title: Keys stay on the server
statement: Keep keys, rationales, rubrics and correction routes off the learner's device, even hidden, until each response is submitted, and score on the server, never trusting the screen's correctness flag.
detail: The reading project's standing rule is that the client renders and reports responses and the server scores (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/BRIEFING.md`). A custom delivery app fetches items in a student-before-answer view, forbids client scoring with a CI gate and rejects client-sent outcomes at its broker (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0060-incept-read-app-field-notebook.qmd`), and a change to the main reading app scores each response on the server from the item's own declarations and never trusts client-reported correctness (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0024-beyond-alpharead-pr45-all-qti-types.qmd`).
against: The lesson engine's animated export still writes each choice question's key into the lesson data its player loads (`g9/transformer/src/glue/animated.js`). The acceptance record marks it as shown in one unit's demonstration, with runtime unverified (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/apush/review/evidence/incept-acceptance.json`). A later run found: both of the lesson engine's exports still put answer material in the page: a 3D version's checkpoint table carries each quick check's expected answer, and an animated version's pages send their own rubric with each answer they ask to be judged (`g9/transformer/test/threejs-render.test.mjs`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/incept-read-app/docs/DOSE-DATA-IN-TIMEBACK.md`).

evidence.quote: **No client-side scoring, ever** — render + report responses; the server scores. Never send renderer outcomes.

The client must **never** extract the answer key, compute score/mastery/XP/accuracy/advancement, send `rendererOutcomes`, persist scores, or hold a secret. QTI is fetched `view=student-before-answer`.
